newsitem.title: UK: NatWest Ventures has record 1996, sees good 1997.
newsitem.headline: NatWest Ventures has record 1996, sees good 1997.

text.p: NatWest Ventures, the venture capital arm of Britain's National Westminster Bank Plc, invested 285 million pounds in 1996 compared with 140 million pounds in 1995. "Looking ahead, we expect the investment environment to remain challenging, but anticipate that there will be no shortage of transactions as corporates continue to focus on disposals of non-core activities," David Shaw, NatWest Ventures chief executive, said in a statement on Tuesday. NatWest Ventures said it had participated in fewer, larger transactions in 1996 and participated in deals worth 1.2 billion pounds.

Among major deals this year, the company was involved in the 171 million pound acquisition of Brent Walker's Pubmaster subsidiary and expanded into continental Europe with new offices in Milan and Dusseldorf. "We now have teams on the ground in all the major European markets and anticipate that, over time, our European business will play and increasingly important role within the group," said European director Chris McCann. -- David Chance, London Newsroom 44 171 542 5887
